quotes.text: Use Terminal to collect inputs from your customers.

old_evidence.text: Don’t use `collect_inputs` to collect sensitive data (including protected health information and customer payment card information), or any information restricted by law.
After the customer has completed all the inputs, the reader changes to a transitional state for 3 seconds, waiting for a subsequent request.
This includes timeouts, which occur after the reader screen isn’t touched for 2 minutes.
Stripe stores the signature images you collect for 7 days.
You can collect customer information even when the smart reader is [operating offline]

findings: The 2026-11-07 canonical capture is a five-variant index with a one-sentence purpose. It verifies navigation to the Server-driven, JavaScript, iOS, Android and React Native variants only. The 2026-05-01 capture supplies the functional content and its filename suffix is not its capture date.

The May capture lists Stripe Reader S700/S710 and BBPOS WisePOS E, supports forms before payment, after payment or outside the payment cycle, and documents six input types. A smart reader displays the first requested input, accepts or allows skipping optional inputs, waits three seconds after completion and returns to splash when no subsequent request arrives. SDK paragraphs specify up to five sequential inputs and the server-driven section documents the required/optional sequence.

In the May capture, server-driven collection is a reader action. Stripe delivers success/failure webhooks to the configured backend, optionally correlates metadata and documents a reader-retrieval fallback. A server-driven inactivity timeout is two minutes, and a completed signature is a file ID for a retrievable SVG stored for seven days. JavaScript/React Native return a promise and iOS/Android a callback. The SDK signatures are SVG strings, SDK toggles can be skipped, and cancel, timeout or another error produces an SDK error.

May gives iOS 4.4.0+ and Android 4.3.0+ and documents collecting while a qualified smart reader is operating offline for iOS, Android and React Native. May supplies no general JavaScript or server-driven offline evidence and no React Native minimum. Keep the sensitive-data prohibition and the merchant's responsibility for applicable consents, contract/notice enforceability, and lawful signature handling.
historical_claims_to_preserve: The prior source provides full dated behavior, including reader models, customer interaction, API/SDK response distinctions, customization, timeout, signature retention and responsibility conditions. Preserve it in Raw Sources and label the November raw as a variant index.

Server-driven may use retrieval as a fallback for failed webhook consumption. The webhook example's Basil version is illustrative. The five-input limit is explicitly documented in SDK sections. Keep SDK versions and offline claims tied to their named platforms.
conflicts: The current summary says M2, WisePad 3 and Tap to Pay are unavailable, while the reviewed May raw explicitly lists supported readers and neither pin expressly states those three exclusions. Use the affirmative dated list unless a separate authority grounds the negative wording.

The current undifferentiated toggle value list combines SDK behavior with the server-driven path. May documents enabled/disabled for server-driven toggles and adds skipped for SDK toggles. Runtime support should not be inferred from the index.
unresolved_questions: The five November links indicate variant routes. Any November changes within them, a reader compatibility matrix beyond the May positive list, and current account/reader eligibility require variant or separate authority.

findings: Add the November raw with a variant-index-only label. Keep the May full capture and all five variant distinctions. Preserve existing reciprocal Terminal and Collect On-Screen Inputs concept routes and add matching source-side links where missing.

Correct the existing summary independently of the index: restore the sensitive-data prohibition, qualify the device list, two-minute timeout, five-input SDK limit and seven-day server-driven signature retention, distinguish toggle responses, and include documented React Native offline support.
conflicts: The pins list supported smart readers rather than expressly naming unsupported M2/WisePad 3/Tap to Pay. Server-driven and SDK toggle response descriptions differ.
source_assessments.reason: The November capture supplies useful variant navigation only. The dated May full capture remains the factual evidence and supports bounded corrections to the existing summary.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/collect-inputs, source-stripe-terminal-collect-inputs has May functional evidence and a November navigation reference. The November capture states the purpose of collecting customer input with Terminal and lists Server-driven, JavaScript, iOS, Android and React Native, without details on supported readers, prerequisites, API or reader transitions (new raw line 7, new raw lines 9-17). The May capture names S700/S710 and BBPOS WisePOS E, allows forms before or after payment or outside a payment cycle, and bars sensitive data. The reader displays the first input, the customer completes or skips optional inputs, and the reader waits three seconds after completion before returning to the splash screen if no request arrives (old raw lines 8-21, old raw lines 128-142). The merchant's server-driven integration starts the reader action and can receive success/failure webhooks, including a failure after two minutes of no touch. An SDK integration instead gets results directly in a promise or callback, and documents up to five sequential inputs. Signatures are retrievable SVG via a file ID in server-driven or an SVG string in the SDK (old raw lines 140-171, old raw line 181, old raw lines 263-273, old raw lines 309-316, old raw lines 445-452, old raw lines 600-606). The summary captures the general flows but should qualify its explicit device exclusions, distinguish SDK and server-driven toggle states, restore the sensitive-data warning, and preserve the May merchant consent and legal responsibility (old raw lines 8-21, old raw lines 134-148, old raw lines 261-273).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/collect-inputs, add a raw_reference to source-stripe-terminal-collect-inputs for the November 7 capture. Its five links replace bundled variant text at the capture level and establish no retirement, availability change, or amended runtime rule (new raw lines 9-17, old raw lines 23-29, old raw lines 173-181, old raw lines 305-316, old raw lines 441-452, old raw lines 596-606). Retain May 1 as the date of factual documentation, including iOS 4.4.0+ and Android 4.3.0+ and smart-reader offline collection for iOS, Android and React Native. Preserve server-driven two-minute no-touch timeout, seven-day Stripe signature file retention, and qualified data-handling and merchant-responsibility warnings (old raw lines 8-21, old raw lines 132-171, old raw lines 309-316, old raw lines 445-452, old raw lines 600-606). Server-driven documents enabled/disabled toggles, while the SDK also documents skipped (old raw lines 142-148, old raw lines 263-273). Keep reciprocal routes to stripe-terminal-collect-inputs and stripe-terminal, using the May raw as behavior evidence and the November index for platform navigation.
